notes: 1. URL = /admin/cms. The sidebar item labelled "Config" opens THIS module (page title "Configurations"). The slug "/admin/cms" is retained from the module's former "CMS" name; /admin/config is not yet a route (302-redirects to /admin/customers).

2. SCOPE GUARD: the separate sidebar item "CMS" opens an external Strapi portal at manage-uat.xrportal.in and is EXCLUDED entirely (CLAUDE.md constraint #2). No TC tests it except ADM_CFG_049 which only confirms the two are distinct.
3. GHNG = registration-number prefix (e.g. GHNG-1000008563-A); a sub-registration suffix is -A/-B/-C.
4. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] = a disposable UAT record/unit/SM-row/tower must be supplied before executing this test.
5. [VERIFY WITH DEV] = behaviour not confirmed in BRD/FRD/FS; confirm before treating Pass/Fail as authoritative.

6. DESTRUCTIVE-LIVE WARNING: every Submit / Update / Save on this page changes LIVE config or cancels LIVE bookings/registrations immediately (only Tower Configuration requires an explicit save click). Per CLAUDE.md Pipeline Discipline #7, do NOT click Submit/Update/Save on a fixture without explicit user authorisation. Where possible the TC asserts the OPEN/un-saved state only.

7. The page has 9 stacked sections (single long scroll): 1 Tower Configuration, 2 Registration Status, 3 Unit Status, 4 Unit Cost Update, 5 Bulk Booking Cancellation, 6 Bulk Registration Cancellation, 7 Sales Managers, 8 Customer Actions Card, 9 Max Preferences Per Unit. Each upload section has its OWN Upload File + Submit button — always scroll to the correct section before clicking.
8. Bulk uploads are SILENT by design (FS §8 of every feature + BRD §11): no SMS/WhatsApp/email is dispatched on save or cancellation. Asserting "no notification" is a required case, not an omission.
9. KNOWN BUG_010 (open): Registration Status (S2) Submit without selecting a file shows no validation error (silent failure). ADM_CFG_015 asserts the buggy actual behaviour.

10. Backend latest-correction values (BRD/FRD §11, dated 2026-05-21) OVERRIDE older FRD/FS body text where they conflict. S4 real columns = allocationAmount/allocationPercent/allocationCalcType (NOT Agreement_Value/EarlyBird); S3 transitions strictly AVAILABLE<->RESERVED (BOOKED->AVAILABLE rejected); S5 cancelable status = WINNER only; S8 "2 Bed Peak Home" is server-force-disabled. See coverage-matrix DOC_DRIFT-001..006.

11. Execution-order convention: read/landing TCs first, then per-section in page order (S1..S9), then cross-section downloads, then API/DB-layer FSD-series, then negative/error. Authoring leaves cols 10-12 (Actual/Status/Tester) blank.

tcs.expected: The client projectId is ignored; the env-resolved projectId is used (BRD §11.1, formerly-accepted req.body.projectId now commented out).

tcs.scenario: [DB] [BUG-REF: BUG-CFG-002] To verify updateCustomerActions has no wrapping transaction
tcs.description: Verify the partial-commit risk: updateCustomerActions writes without a wrapping DB transaction.
tcs.precond: A valid admin JWT; ability to force a mid-write failure (dev). NO-VISUAL-EVIDENCE — DB layer.
tcs.steps:
1. Trigger a Customer Actions update that fails part-way through (forced).
2. Inspect which fields persisted.
tcs.expected: [VERIFY WITH DEV] — without a wrapping transaction, a mid-write failure can leave a partial commit. Record actual persisted state and confirm intended atomicity with dev.

tcs.scenario: [API] [FSD-CORRECTION] To verify /master-config/fetch is not admin-only
tcs.description: Verify the auth gap that /master-config/fetch is reachable by any authenticated user, not admin-only.
tcs.precond: A non-admin authenticated token is available. NO-VISUAL-EVIDENCE — API layer.
tcs.steps:
1. Call /master-config/fetch with a non-admin authenticated token.
2. Observe the response.
tcs.expected: The endpoint returns config data to any authenticated user (auth gap). [VERIFY WITH DEV] whether this is intended; flag as a security finding.

tcs.scenario: To verify Customer Actions save sends no notification
tcs.description: Verify the Customer Actions update is silent (FS Feature 8 §8).
tcs.precond: An admin saved a Customer Actions change; user authorisation.
tcs.steps:

2. Verify no notification is dispatched.
tcs.expected: No SMS / WhatsApp / email is sent (silent by design, FS Feature 8 §8).

tcs.scenario: To verify Customer Portal enforces new settings (integration)
tcs.description: Verify that a saved Customer Actions configuration is enforced immediately on the Customer Portal.
tcs.precond: An admin saved a Customer Actions change; user authorisation.
tcs.steps:
1. Save a typology/master change in Section 8.
2. On the Customer Portal, attempt an additional registration for the affected typology.
tcs.expected: The Customer Portal immediately reflects the new allow/block + count limits (FS Feature 8 §7, BRD §8 Customers dependency).

tcs.scenario: To verify Section 9 shows the current Max Preferences value
tcs.description: Verify the read-only current value of the Max Preferences Per Unit select.
tcs.precond: An admin is on the Max Preferences Per Unit section.
tcs.steps:
1. Scroll to 'Max Preferences Per Unit'.
2. Read the current select value and helper text.
tcs.expected: The select shows the current value (6 on UAT) with helper 'Set the maximum number of preferences a user can select for each unit' and an Update button.

tcs.scenario: To verify the full control inventory of Max Preferences
tcs.description: Verify Section 9 has exactly the value select and one Update button.
tcs.precond: An admin is on the Max Preferences Per Unit section.
tcs.steps: 1. Enumerate every control without changing or saving.
tcs.expected: One value select and one 'Update' button (note: Update, not Submit). No other controls.

tcs.scenario: To verify changing Max Preferences via Update
tcs.description: Verify that selecting a new value and clicking Update persists the change.
tcs.precond: An admin has user authorisation for a Config write.
tcs.steps:
1. Change the select from 6 to 10.
2. Click 'Update'.
3. Reload and re-read.
tcs.expected: The new value (10) persists after reload (FS Feature 9 §7).

tcs.scenario: To verify the valid range 0-255
tcs.description: Verify the boundary that Max Preferences accepts values from 0 to 255 (BRD §6 rule 10).
tcs.precond: An admin is on the Max Preferences Per Unit section.
tcs.steps:
1. Open the value select and note its range.
2. (If editable) test the 0 and 255 boundaries.
tcs.expected: Valid range is 0 to 255 (BRD §6 rule 10). Boundary values 0 and 255 are accepted.

tcs.scenario: To verify an out-of-range value (>255) is rejected
tcs.description: Verify behaviour when a value above 255 is attempted (if the control allows it).
tcs.precond: An admin can attempt an out-of-range value (UI or API); user authorisation.
tcs.steps:
1. Attempt to set the value to 256 (or higher) via the UI/API.
2. Click Update / submit and observe.
tcs.expected: [VERIFY WITH DEV] — if the select caps at 255 the UI prevents it; confirm the API also rejects >255 (BRD §6 rule 10 implies a 0-255 cap).

tcs.scenario: To verify a no-change Update
tcs.description: Verify the behaviour of clicking Update without changing the value.
tcs.precond: An admin is on Section 9; user authorisation.
tcs.steps:
1. Without changing the value, click 'Update'.
2. Observe.
tcs.expected: [VERIFY WITH DEV] — record whether the no-op Update succeeds silently or returns a 'No Change' response (parallel to S8 §11.3).

tcs.scenario: To verify reducing the limit does not invalidate existing preferences
tcs.description: Verify that lowering Max Preferences does not retroactively remove preferences already submitted (BRD §6 rule 10).
tcs.precond: A buyer already has more preferences than the new lower cap; user authorisation.
tcs.steps:
1. Lower the Max Preferences value below an existing buyer's preference count.
2. Update.
3. Inspect that buyer's existing preferences.
tcs.testData: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] buyer with prefs above the new cap
tcs.expected: Existing preferences are preserved; only NEW preference additions are capped (BRD §6 rule 10).

tcs.scenario: To verify Max Preferences save sends no notification
tcs.description: Verify the Max Preferences update is silent (FS Feature 9 §8).

tcs.expected: No notification is dispatched (silent by design, FS Feature 9 §8).

tcs.scenario: [API] To verify the Max Preferences update endpoint
tcs.description: Verify that PUT /api/v1/admin/max-preferences-per-unit/:projectId persists the value (API path behind Section 9).

tcs.scenario: To verify the cap is enforced in Allocation selection (integration)
tcs.description: Verify that the Max Preferences value caps how many unit preferences a buyer can select during a campaign.
tcs.precond: A buyer in an allocation session; the cap is set to a low value; user authorisation.
tcs.steps:
1. Set Max Preferences to a low value (e.g. 2).
2. In an allocation session, attempt to select more than the cap.
tcs.expected: The buyer is blocked from selecting more preferences than the cap (BRD §8 Allocation dependency).

tcs.scenario: To verify each section has its own Upload and Submit buttons
tcs.description: Verify that the six upload sections each have their own scoped Upload File and Submit buttons (no shared button).
tcs.precond: An admin is on the Configurations page.
tcs.steps:

2. Confirm each has its own Upload File and Submit button.
tcs.expected: Sections 2,3,4,5,6,7 each expose their own Upload File + Submit; section 8 has Submit; section 9 has Update. Clicking the wrong section's button processes the wrong upload (BRD §5 warning).

tcs.scenario: [API] To verify a bulk upload error returns an Excel error file with HTTP 400
tcs.description: Verify that when a bulk upload has errors the system returns a per-row error Excel with HTTP 400, not a generic toast (BRD §6 rule 11).
tcs.precond: A valid admin JWT and a file with mixed valid/invalid rows. NO-VISUAL-EVIDENCE — API layer.
tcs.steps:
1. Submit a bulk upload (e.g. Unit Cost / SM) containing invalid rows.
2. Inspect the HTTP status and the returned file.
tcs.expected: HTTP 400 with a downloadable Excel file showing per-row error detail (BRD §6 rule 11).
